messages:
maria: Heads-up — Acme POC reports exported logs into Splunk are missing trace IDs (trace_id field empty) after we enabled their log-drain. Also hitting 429s from our /v1/logs/drain endpoint when they push ~8MB/s. Can eng help triage?
aj: On it. Are the 429s originating from Redwood's API gateway or from the drain forwarder (Splunk side)? Any sample errors?
maria: 429s appear in our API logs: `rate_limit_exceeded` for the drain route. Splunk shows events but `trace_id` is blank for many events. Sample log below.
maria: ```
{"ts":"2026-03-20T17:12:34Z","service":"ingest-forwarder","msg":"event","trace_id":"","request_id":"req_9f2a","body":{"user":"u123","action":"complete"}}
```
oliver: Two things to check: 1) the agent/SDK must propagate the trace header (we expect `X-Trace-ID` or `traceparent`) and the drain template needs `{{trace_id}}`. 2) 429s can be smoothed by a temporary quota bump for the POC while we debug.
sophie: Also confirm the runtime batching config isn't stripping request headers during batching. On some older runtime builds `batch.keep_headers` defaulted to false. Please verify `redwood.runtime.batch.keep_headers: true`.
aj: Quick tests we can run: 
1) curl with header: `curl -H "X-Trace-ID: 1234abcd" -d '{"msg":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/logs/drain` — verify downstream event contains `trace_id: 1234abcd`.
2) Check drain template in Console: Route -> Integrations -> Log drains -> Template should include `{{trace_id}}` or `{{request.headers.X-Trace-ID}}`.
maria: customer is using a Fluentd forwarder, their current drain template only references `{{request.id}}` and `{{body}}` — no trace substitution.
aj: That explains missing traces. If Fluentd can add the header mapping we should see trace_id populated. For the 429s, I can temporarily raise the drain rate limit for their account while we fix the template.
ryan: I just opened a quota bump: POC-EXPORT-4567, increased drain throughput 2x for 24h. Will monitor. :white_check_mark:
aj: Thanks. After bump, run the `curl` test above and paste the resulting downstream line. If `trace_id` still blank, paste the raw HTTP request we receive.
maria: Customer ran curl test with header and Splunk still shows blank trace_id for some events — they pasted one raw request and I forwarded to you.
aj: Looking at the raw: the forwarder is overwriting headers when batching multiple events. Suggest two fixes: 1) set `batch.keep_headers: true` in runtime config, or 2) modify forwarder to inject `trace_id` into the event body before batching.
sophie: Also check sampling rules — if trace sampling <100% some spans/traces might be dropped downstream. For narrow POC debugging set Console -> Observability -> Traces sampling override = 100%.
oliver: FYI on pricing: exporting full traces at 100% will increase billable data outward. For rough numbers: ~1M traces/day with full payload ~ 20GB/day egress -> estimate we'll DM a cost delta.
maria: Customer agreed to change template and enable header passthrough. After we do that and keep the quota bump, can we reconvene in ~2 hours?
aj: Yes. I'll push a small config change to enable `batch.keep_headers` on their runtime instance and restart the forwarder. Deploy-bot will show status.
deploy-bot: config apply started for account acme-poc; change id ch_8921; rolling restart.
ryan: Deploy finished, watching metrics. 429s dropped to near-zero. Traces are now mostly populated in Splunk but a few legacy events still missing `trace_id` due to older forwarded payloads.
maria: Great progress — I'll let the customer know and ask them to re-run their ingestion tests.
aj: Follow-ups: (1) Confirm Fluentd template updated to include `{{request.headers.X-Trace-ID}}` or inline `{{trace_id}}` mapping. (2) Keep sampling at 100% for 24h, then revert. (3) Close POC-EXPORT-4567 after 24h monitoring unless more issues.
oliver: I'll prepare a short note about the temporary quota bump and a cost estimate for the customer procurement team.
maria: Thanks team — will update customer and mark this thread. If anything else shows up I'll ping here. :pray:
